# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

It was only on the following Friday that Thirza was told the tale about the hat covered in flowers. Upon her return from the house of Mrs. Sowerby, she demanded an explanation from Nell.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0000 }

“Nell, Mrs. Agatha says you attended church this past Sunday wearing a hat absurdly adorned with roses and buttercups. Whatever possessed you to pull a stunt like that? You must have looked quite sightly!”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0001 }

“Oh. I am aware that pink and yellow do not look good on me,” Nell started.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0002 }

“Nonsense to speak of becoming! What proved ridiculous was placing any flowers whatsoever upon your hat, regardless of their hue. You are an exceedingly infuriating child!”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0003 }

“I fail to understand how wearing flowers on a hat is any more absurd than on a dress,” Nell objected. “A great number of young girls present had flowers fastened to their dresses. Where is the distinction?”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0004 }

Thirza refused to be led away from the secure realm of the concrete toward the uncertain routes of the abstract.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0005 }

“Do not respond to me in that manner, Nell. Doing that was an extremely foolish action on your part. Do not ever allow me to catch you playing such a prank again. Mrs. Agatha mentions that she felt as though she would sink through the floor the moment she witnessed you arrive all dressed up in that fashion. She was unable to approach you closely enough to instruct you to remove them until the opportunity had passed. She states that the gossip among people was quite terrible. Naturally, they would assume I lacked the good judgment to prevent you from going out adorned in such a way.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0006 }

“Oh, I’m so sorry,” said Nell, as tears began filling her eyes. “I never imagined it would bother you. I felt they would look charming on my hat because the buttercups and roses were so sweet and pretty. Artificial flowers were worn on the hats of many of the little girls. I fear I will turn out to be a terrible trial for you. Perhaps returning me to the asylum would be best for you. It would be awful; enduring it seems impossible for me; I would probably develop consumption; you can see how thin I am already, after all. Still, it would be preferable to being a trial for you.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0007 }

“Nonsense,” stated Thirza, annoyed with herself because she had caused the child to weep. “I am certain that I have no desire to return you to the asylum. My sole wish is for you to conduct yourself as other little girls do and refrain from making yourself look foolish. Stop weeping now. There is some news I have for you. Isolde Pembroke arrived home this afternoon. I am heading up there to find out whether I can borrow a skirt pattern from Mrs. Pembroke, and you may accompany me and become acquainted with Isolde if you wish.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0008 }

Nell stood up, her hands folded together and tears yet shining upon her cheeks, while the dish towel she was in the middle of hemming slid unnoticed down to the floor.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0009 }

“Oh, Thirza, I am filled with fear—at present that the moment has arrived, I am genuinely afraid. Suppose she fails to be fond of me! That would stand as the most tragic letdown I have ever experienced.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0010 }

“There now, try not to become flustered. Furthermore, I really hope you will refrain from employing such lengthy vocabulary. Coming from such a small girl, it comes across as quite strange. It is my belief that Isolde will find you pleasant enough. However, the person you must truly account for is her mother. Should she take a dislike to you, Isolde’s affection for you will be of no consequence. In the event that she has been informed of your angry display toward Mrs. Sowerby and your attendance at church wearing buttercups around your headwear, I cannot imagine what opinion she will hold regarding you. It is essential that you remain courteous and act properly, and avoid delivering any of your shocking remarks. Goodness gracious, the child is truly shaking!”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0011 }

Nell shuddered, her pale face stretched tight.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0012 }

“Oh, Thirza, had you been about to encounter a young girl you desired to have as your closest companion and whose mother perhaps would not approve of you, excitement would overcome you as well,” she uttered while hurrying to retrieve her hat.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0013 }

Taking the shortcut over the brook and through the fir-tree grove, they made their way to Pear Hill. Thirza knocked on the kitchen door, which was answered by Mrs. Pembroke. Possessing a remarkably determined mouth, she was a tall woman with dark eyes and dark hair. She was known to be extremely firm when it came to her children.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0014 }

“In what manner do you fare, Thirza?” she inquired warmly. “Enter. Further, I presume this represents the small female child you have taken as your own?”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0015 }

“Indeed, Nell Harcourt is who this is,” Thirza declared.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0016 }

“Spelled with an E,” gasped Nell, who, despite being excited and tremulous, was resolute that no misunderstanding should exist regarding that crucial detail.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0017 }

Failing to hear or perhaps not understanding, Mrs. Pembroke simply clasped hands and remarked gently:
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0018 }

“How are you?”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0019 }

“Thank you ma’am, my physical health is fine, even if my mood is quite disheveled,” Nell stated seriously. After that, she turned toward Thirza and whispered loud enough to be heard, “Thirza, that wasn't particularly shocking, was it?”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0020 }

A book was being read by Isolde as she sat on the sofa, but she let it fall upon the arrival of the visitors. A extremely attractive young girl, she possessed the dark eyes and hair of her mother, along with cheeks of rose, while her cheerful look came to her as a legacy from her father.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0021 }

“This is Isolde, my little girl,” Mrs. Pembroke said. “Isolde, perhaps you can show Nell your flowers out in the garden. Doing that will be far better for you than making your eyes suffer over that book. She spends way too much time reading—” she remarked to Thirza while the young girls stepped outside—“and I am unable to stop her, because her father encourages and helps her. A book is something she is constantly reading. Having the possibility of a playmate makes me happy—maybe she will spend more time outside because of it.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0022 }

Nell and Isolde were standing out in the garden, which was filled with the soft light of the setting sun shining through the dark, ancient fir trees located to its west, and they looked at one another bashfully across a patch of splendid tiger lilies.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0023 }

A bowery wilderness of flowers, the Pembroke garden would have gladdened Nell’s heart during any period less charged with fate. Enclosing it were massive old willows and lofty firs, under which blossomed shade-loving flora. Crisp, right-angled walkways neatly edged with clamshells crossed it such as damp red ribbons, and old-fashioned blooms grew profusely in the intervening beds. Rosy bleeding-hearts were present alongside grand, magnificent crimson peonies; white, sweet-scented narcissi stood with prickly, sweet Scotch roses; columbines of pink, blue, and white grew near lilac-shaded Bouncing Bets; there were clusters of southernwood, ribbon grass, and mint; purple Adam-and-Eve appeared with daffodils and aggregations of sweet clover pale with its dainty, aromatic, feathery plumes; scarlet lightning thrust its flaming spears above demure white musk-flowers; it was a garden in which sunshine rested and bees droned, and breezes, coaxed to linger, purred and rustled.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0024 }

“Oh, Isolde,” Nell uttered finally, holding her hands together and uttering the words barely above a breath, “oh, do you believe you could fondle me slightly—sufficiently to become my dearest companion?”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0025 }

Isolde burst into laughter, as she invariably did prior to uttering a word.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0026 }

“Well, I suppose that’s true,” she stated openly. “I am so happy that you have moved to Grey Shutters. Having a companion to play with will be wonderful. No other girls reside close enough for us to play together, and none of my sisters are old enough.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0027 }

“Will you promise to be my friend for all time?” Nell asked with eagerness.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0028 }

Isolde looked shocked.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0029 }

“The act of swearing is remarkably evil, after all,” she stated with a tone of rebuke.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0030 }

“Oh no, my sort of swearing isn't that. You know there exist two types.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0031 }

“I only ever knew of a single type,” Isolde remarked with hesitation.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0032 }

“Another one truly exists. Oh, it is not evil in any way. It merely involves making a solemn vow and promise.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0033 }

“Indeed, I am fine with performing that,” consented Isolde, feeling a sense of relief. “In what way do you accomplish it?”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0034 }

“We must clasp hands—like this,” Nell said with gravity. “It should take place above flowing water. We will simply pretend this trail is flowing water. First, I will say the vow. I solemnly swear to remain loyal to my bosom friend, Isolde Pembroke, for as long as the sun and moon endure. Now repeat it yourself and insert my name.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0035 }

Laughter echoing from both bow and stern, Isolde reiterated the “oath.” She subsequently remarked:
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0036 }

“Nell, you are an unusual girl. I had previously been told that you were unusual. Even so, it seems to me that I am going to be very fond of you.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0037 }

As far as the log bridge, Isolde accompanied Thirza and Nell on their walk home. Embracing each other, the pair of young girls strolled along. Upon reaching the brook, they separated, having made numerous pledges to meet again the following afternoon.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0038 }

“Well, did you find Isolde a kindred spirit?” Thirza inquired while they ascended through the garden at Grey Shutters.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0039 }

“Indeed,” Nell breathed out, entirely unaware that Thirza was being sarcastic. “Oh Thirza, right now no girl on St. Brendan’s Island feels more joy than I do. You can be certain that I will offer my prayers with genuine gladness this evening. Isolde and I plan to construct a playhouse tomorrow within the birch grove belonging to Mr. William Bell. May I take the fragments of smashed china located in the woodshed? February brings Isolde’s birthday, whereas my own falls in March. Wouldn't you agree that such a timing is an exceptionally odd coincidence? Isolde intends to loan me a volume for reading. It is absolutely wonderful and intensely thrilling, according to her. She will point out a spot deep among the trees where rice lilies can be found. Wouldn't you say that Isolde possesses exceedingly soulful eyes? It would be wonderful if my own eyes were soulful. Isolde plans to instruct me in singing a piece entitled ‘Nelly in the Hazel Dell.’ She means to present me with an illustration to display inside my bedroom; according to her, it is a truly magnificent image—a exquisite woman wearing a gown of pale blue silk. It was presented to her by a representative selling sewing machines. It breaks my heart that I possess nothing to present to Isolde. My height exceeds Isolde’s by an inch, yet her body is considerably plumper; she claims a desire to be slender due to it being far more elegant, though I suspect she merely made that statement to comfort my emotions. At some point, we plan to visit the beach to collect seashells. We settled on naming the stream near the log bridge the Nymph’s Well. Would you not call that a supremely sophisticated name? I previously read a tale featuring a spring bearing that title. It is my belief that a dryad resembles an adult fairy.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0040 }

“Well, my sole wish is that Isolde isn't talked to death by you,” Thirza remarked. “However, Nell, bear this in mind throughout your preparations. Your time won't be spent playing entirely, or even for the greater part of it. Your tasks will await you, and completing them must come before anything else.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0041 }

Nell’s joy was complete, and Obed made it spill over. Having recently returned from a journey to the Delford store, he awkwardly drew a little package out of his pocket and presented it to Nell, casting an apologetic glance toward Thirza.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0042 }

“I brought you these because I overheard you mention that you enjoyed chocolate sweeties,” he said.
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0043 }

“Humph,” Thirza sniffed. “It is going to destroy her stomach and teeth. Now, now, child, do not appear so gloomy. Since Obed went out and purchased them, you may consume those. It would have been preferable if he had carried peppermints to you. Those are more wholesome. Do not make yourself ill by consuming every one of them right away now.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0044 }

“Oh, no, indeed, I won’t,” Thirza was eagerly told by Nell. “I’ll just consume a single one this evening, Thirza. And half of them can be given to Isolde by me, can’t they? To me, the remaining half will taste doubly sweet if a portion is bestowed upon her. Thinking that I possess something to present to her brings me great joy.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0045 }

“To give the girl her due,” Thirza remarked after Nell retired to her gable, “selfishness isn’t in her nature. That pleases me, because a penny-pinching child is something I find particularly repulsive. Goodness, she arrived merely three weeks ago, yet it feels as though her presence here has been lifelong. The household seems unthinkable without her now. Now, refrain from giving me that triumphant expression, Obed. Such behavior is intolerable enough when a woman does it, but from a man, it cannot be borne at all. I am entirely ready to admit my satisfaction at agreeing to harbor the girl and my growing affection toward her, but do not taunt me with it, Obed Abernethy.”
{: #nw-v01-c12-p0046 }
